question:
As of April 10, 2025: A household has $140 in monthly gross income and $90 in a checking account. Is it entitled to expedited service?
A. Only if it is a migrant or seasonal farmworker household
B. No: gross income must be under $100
C. Only if its rent exceeds its income
D. Yes: gross income under $150 and liquid resources of $100 or less
E. No: liquid resources must be $0

As of September 3, 2025: A household has $160 in monthly gross income and $50 in savings. Its rent is $800 a month and its utility allowance is $300. Is it entitled to expedited service?
A. Yes: its income plus liquid resources ($210) is less than its rent and utilities ($1,100)
B. No: its gross income is not under $150
C. Only if it applied after the 15th of the month
D. Only if every member is elderly or disabled
E. No: its liquid resources must be under $25

As of February 11, 2026: A household has $140 in monthly gross income and $250 in a bank account. Its rent and utilities total $300 a month. Is it entitled to expedited service?
A. No: its liquid resources exceed $100 and its income plus resources ($390) exceed its rent and utilities
B. Only if it has a member over 60
C. Yes: its gross income is under $150
D. Yes: its rent is under $400
E. Yes: any household under $500 in resources qualifies

As of July 20, 2024: A household's monthly gross income is $900 and it has $400 in savings. Its rent is $1,100 and its utility allowance is $350. Is it entitled to expedited service?
A. No: savings over $100 never qualify
B. Only if it is destitute
C. Only after a 30-day wait
D. No: income over $150 never qualifies
E. Yes: its income plus liquid resources ($1,300) is less than its rent and utilities ($1,450)

As of May 5, 2025: A household's only elderly member pays $210 a month in unreimbursed medical costs. What is the excess medical deduction?
A. $210
B. $0
C. $175
D. $185
E. $35

As of January 22, 2026: A 40-year-old household member who is neither elderly nor disabled pays $300 a month in medical costs; no one else has medical costs. What is the excess medical deduction?
A. $35
B. $300
C. $0: only elderly or disabled members' costs count
D. $265
E. $150

As of March 1, 2025: A household with no elderly or disabled member has $600 a month of income after all other deductions and $1,500 a month in shelter costs. What is its excess shelter deduction in the 48 contiguous states?
A. $1,500
B. $1,200
C. $900
D. $600
E. $712 (the cap)

As of March 1, 2025: A household that includes a disabled member has $600 a month of income after all other deductions and $1,500 a month in shelter costs. What is its excess shelter deduction?
A. $900
B. $300
C. $1,500
D. $1,200: no cap for a household with an elderly or disabled member
E. $712

As of August 14, 2025: A household with no elderly or disabled member has $1,000 a month of income after all other deductions and $900 in shelter costs. What is its excess shelter deduction?
A. $900
B. $712
C. $450
D. $0
E. $400

As of August 1, 2026: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, can a household's monthly internet service fee be counted in its excess shelter deduction?
A. Yes, up to $50 a month
B. Only for households with school-age children
C. No
D. Only if the state's utility allowance does not include it
E. Yes, as a utility
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 5(e)(6)

question:
As of June 1, 2025: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, is a 56-year-old able-bodied adult without dependents subject to the ABAWD time limit?
A. Yes: there is no age exception
B. Yes: the exception starts at 65
C. Yes: the exception starts at 60
D. No: in fiscal year 2025 the exception covers people over 55
E. No: the exception starts at 50
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 6(o)(3)

question:
As of June 1, 2025: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, is a 54-year-old able-bodied adult without dependents subject to the ABAWD time limit?
A. No: ABAWD rules end at 52
B. No: the exception covers people over 49
C. Yes: in fiscal year 2025 the age exception covers only people over 55
D. No: the time limit was repealed
E. No: the exception covers people over 50
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 6(o)(3)

question:
As of August 1, 2026: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, is a 60-year-old able-bodied adult without dependents subject to the ABAWD time limit?
A. Yes: the age exception now covers only people over 65
B. No: the time limit applies only under 50
C. No: the exception covers people over 55
D. No: the exception covers people over 59
E. No: the exception covers people 60 and older
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 6(o)(3)

question:
As of August 1, 2026: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, a parent's youngest child in the household is 15. Is the parent excepted from the ABAWD time limit because of the child?
A. No: parents are never excepted
B. Yes: any child under 16 qualifies
C. Yes: any child under 18 qualifies
D. No: the exception covers responsibility for a dependent child under 14
E. Yes: any dependent child of any age qualifies
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 6(o)(3)

question:
As of August 1, 2026: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, which of these is still listed as an exception to the ABAWD time limit?
A. A veteran
B. A pregnant woman
C. A homeless individual
D. A 22-year-old who aged out of foster care
E. A person over 55
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 6(o)(3)

question:
As of June 1, 2025: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, which of these people is excepted from the ABAWD time limit?
A. A 50-year-old in fiscal year 2025
B. A 23-year-old who was in foster care at age 18
C. A 45-year-old who works 10 hours a week
D. A 30-year-old who was in foster care at age 15 only
E. A 40-year-old full-time student
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 6(o)(3)

question:
As of November 1, 2025: An able-bodied adult without dependents works 15 hours a week and volunteers in a state work program 6 hours a week. Do they meet the ABAWD work requirement?
A. No: they must work 30 hours a week
B. Yes: work and a work program can be combined to reach 20 hours a week
C. No: they must work 20 hours in a job alone
D. No: volunteering never counts
E. Yes: any work at all meets the requirement

As of June 20, 2026: In California, a CalFresh application is received on May 29, 2026 and approved on June 8, 2026. Under which ABAWD exemption criteria is the applicant screened?
A. The criteria in force on the approval date
B. No screening is required
C. Whichever favors the applicant
D. The H.R. 1 criteria
E. The pre-H.R. 1 criteria

As of July 1, 2026: In California, an ongoing CalFresh household's recertification was due in May 2026 and its new certification period starts June 1, 2026. Which ABAWD exemption criteria apply at that recertification?
A. The criteria in the county's waiver
B. The pre-H.R. 1 criteria
C. None until the next recertification
D. Both, whichever is stricter
E. The H.R. 1 criteria, because the new period starts June 1

As of July 15, 2026: In California, a household reports on June 3, 2026 that a new member joined. Under which ABAWD exemption criteria is the new member screened?
A. The H.R. 1 criteria, even if other members have not had an H.R. 1 screening
B. Whichever criteria favor the member
C. The criteria in force when the household first applied
D. No screening until the next recertification
E. The pre-H.R. 1 criteria, because the household's other members were screened under them

As of July 15, 2026: In California, a household reports on May 20, 2026 that a new member joined. Under which ABAWD exemption criteria is the new member screened?
A. No screening until the next recertification
B. The criteria in the federal statute as of that date
C. The H.R. 1 criteria
D. The pre-H.R. 1 criteria
E. Whichever criteria favor the member

As of March 15, 2026: In California, can a county assign an ABAWD countable month for March 2026?
A. Yes: the new statewide clock started January 1, 2026
B. No: no countable months may be assigned before June 1, 2026
C. Only for applicants, not ongoing households
D. Only in counties without a waiver
E. Yes: H.R. 1 took effect July 4, 2025

As of November 15, 2026: Is Alpine County, California covered by an ABAWD time limit waiver in November 2026?
A. Yes: until June 1, 2027
B. Yes: the waiver runs through October 31, 2027
C. Yes: all California counties are waived
D. No: its waiver expired October 31, 2026 and it was not included in the new waiver
E. Only for residents over 50

As of May 1, 2026: In California, a CalFresh application is received on March 28, 2026 and processed on April 3, 2026. Which noncitizen eligibility criteria apply?
A. The criteria in effect on the interview date
B. The H.R. 1 criteria, because H.R. 1 took effect July 4, 2025
C. The pre-H.R. 1 criteria
D. The H.R. 1 criteria, because it was processed after April 1
E. Whichever favor the applicant

As of June 1, 2026: In California, when do the H.R. 1 noncitizen rules first apply to an ongoing household?
A. Never; they apply only to new applicants
B. On July 4, 2025
C. Immediately on April 1, 2026, mid-period
D. At its recertification, starting with recertifications due in April 2026 (effective May 1, 2026)
E. At its next periodic report

As of July 15, 2026: In California, will a lawful permanent resident who was eligible for CalFresh before April 1, 2026 remain eligible after April 1, 2026, regardless of how they obtained that status?
A. No, unless they obtained status through employment
B. No, they lose eligibility at the next recertification
C. Yes
D. Only if they have 40 work quarters
E. Only if they are under 18

As of July 1, 2026: In California, from June 1, 2026, may a county require a parolee to have been paroled for at least one year to receive California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) benefits?
A. Yes, one year is required
B. Only in counties without automation
C. No
D. Yes, until the next recertification
E. Yes, but only for new applicants

As of August 1, 2026: In California, a household with a student in a UC bachelor's program has a recertification due in June 2026. When does the new LPIE process apply to it?
A. Only if the student re-applies
B. June 1, 2026, mid-period
C. At its first recertification in 2027
D. Retroactively to January 1, 2026
E. For the certification period effective July 1, 2026

As of May 1, 2026: In California, when does an ongoing CalWORKs/CalFresh family first get the AB 42 exemption for higher-education grants and scholarships?
A. Only at application
B. On July 1, 2026
C. Immediately on March 1, 2026
D. Retroactively to January 1, 2026
E. At its next SAR 7 or recertification after March 1, 2026

As of August 1, 2026: In California, does the AB 320 income exemption change a benefit determination made in May 2026?
A. Yes: it applies back to January 1, 2026
B. Yes: counties must recompute all 2026 benefits
C. No: it does not apply retroactively to determinations made before July 1, 2026
D. Only for CalFresh, not CalWORKs
E. Only if the household requests it

As of February 1, 2025: Since when has California operated its CalFresh Standard Medical Deduction demonstration project?
A. October 1, 2017
B. January 1, 2024
C. October 1, 2021
D. October 1, 2025
E. July 4, 2025

As of July 1, 2026: How does California CalFresh treat Medicare Advantage supplemental benefits (such as plan reimbursements)?
A. They reduce the medical deduction dollar for dollar
B. They are counted as unearned income
C. They are counted as earned income
D. They are counted as a resource
E. They are excluded from income

As of July 1, 2026: Through when are California counties approved to operate the Early Denial Waiver?
A. September 30, 2029
B. April 30, 2026
C. October 31, 2027
D. April 30, 2029
E. June 1, 2026

As of October 15, 2025: For how long did FNS hold states harmless in Quality Control for misapplying the H.R. 1 utility allowance (LIHEAP) change?
A. One year from July 4, 2025
B. 30 days from July 4, 2025
C. There was no hold-harmless period
D. 120 days from July 4, 2025
E. Until October 1, 2026

As of June 1, 2025: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, a household with no elderly or disabled member received a $25 LIHEAP payment last winter. Must the state give it the heating and cooling utility allowance on that basis?
A. No: the payment must exceed $100
B. Yes: a LIHEAP payment over $20 in the current or prior 12 months qualifies any household
C. No: only households with an elderly or disabled member qualify
D. Only if it pays heating costs directly
E. No: LIHEAP no longer affects the allowance
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 5(e)(6)(C)(iv)

question:
As of August 1, 2026: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, a household with no elderly or disabled member received a $25 LIHEAP payment last winter. Must the state give it the heating and cooling utility allowance on that basis?
A. Yes, but only for 12 months
B. Yes: any LIHEAP payment over $20 qualifies
C. Yes: any LIHEAP payment qualifies
D. No: the payment must exceed $50
E. No: the LIHEAP rule now covers only households with an elderly or disabled member
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 5(e)(6)(C)(iv)

question:
As of June 1, 2025: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, a household received a $15 LIHEAP payment last year. Does that payment by itself entitle it to the heating and cooling utility allowance?
A. No: the payment must be greater than $20
B. Yes: but only for 6 months
C. Yes: payments of $10 or more qualify
D. Yes: any LIHEAP payment qualifies
E. Only if it has an elderly member
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 5(e)(6)(C)(iv)

question:
As of September 1, 2026: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, once the cost share applies, what share of benefit costs does a state with a payment error rate of exactly 10.0% pay?
A. 15 percent
B. 0 percent
C. 20 percent
D. 5 percent
E. 10 percent
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 4(a)(2)(B)(i)

question:
As of September 1, 2026: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, once the cost share applies, what share of benefit costs does a state with a payment error rate of 5.9% pay?
A. 2 percent
B. 0 percent
C. 15 percent
D. 10 percent
E. 5 percent
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 4(a)(2)(B)(i)

question:
As of September 1, 2026: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, does a state with a 12% payment error rate pay a share of benefit costs in fiscal year 2027?
A. Yes, 10 percent
B. Yes, 25 percent
C. No: the state share begins in fiscal year 2028
D. Yes, 5 percent
E. Yes, 15 percent
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 4(a)(2)(B)(i)

question:
As of September 1, 2026: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, once the cost share applies, what share of benefit costs does a state with a payment error rate of 7.99% pay?
A. 7.99 percent
B. 10 percent
C. 15 percent
D. 5 percent
E. 0 percent
citation: Food and Nutrition Act of 2008, Sec. 4(a)(2)(B)(i)

question:
As of October 1, 2025: A 19-year-old enrolled half-time at a community college works 15 hours a week, has no children, and meets no other exemption. Can they get SNAP?
A. No: they need 20 paid work hours a week or another exemption
B. Yes: half-time students are not covered by the student rule
C. Yes: community college students are exempt
D. Yes: any paid work qualifies
E. Yes: students under 22 are exempt

As of October 1, 2025: A 25-year-old enrolled full-time cares for her 8-year-old child, and the state has found adequate child care is available. Is she exempt from the student rule because of the child?
A. No: parents are never exempt
B. Yes: any parent of a child under 12 is exempt
C. No: for a child 6 to 11, the exemption applies only when adequate child care is not available
D. Yes: full-time students with children are always exempt
E. Yes: any parent of a child under 18 is exempt

As of October 1, 2025: A 30-year-old student enrolled half-time cares for a 4-year-old household member. Is the student exempt from the student rule?
A. No: only parents of children under 1 are exempt
B. Only if they also work 20 hours
C. Yes: responsible for a dependent household member under 6
D. No: the child must be under 2
E. Only if child care is unavailable

As of October 1, 2025: A 52-year-old enrolled full-time in a graduate program, not working, applies for SNAP. Does the student rule bar them?
A. Yes: they must work 20 hours a week
B. Yes: graduate students are never eligible
C. Yes: the age exemption ends at 50
D. No: students age 50 or older are exempt
E. No: only undergraduates are covered

As of October 1, 2025: A student approved for federal work study expects to work during the term. When does their work-study exemption begin?
A. The month the school term begins or the month work study is approved, whichever is later
B. The day they first get paid
C. At the start of the calendar year
D. Only after they work 20 hours in a week
E. The month after they apply

As of February 1, 2025: A person is found to have committed a second intentional Program violation (no trafficking or other special case). How long are they disqualified?
A. Permanently
B. 24 months
C. 36 months
D. 12 months
E. 6 months

As of February 1, 2025: A person is found to have committed a third intentional Program violation. How long are they disqualified?
A. 36 months
B. Permanently
C. 24 months
D. 10 years
E. 12 months

As of May 1, 2025: A person fails to comply with SNAP work requirements for the second time and complies again right away. What is the shortest federal disqualification period?
A. 6 months
B. 1 month
C. 3 months
D. None, if they comply right away
E. 12 months

As of May 1, 2025: For a third occurrence of noncompliance with SNAP work requirements, which disqualification may a state choose?
A. Permanent disqualification
B. A 30-day warning only
C. Only 1 month
D. No disqualification
E. Only 3 months

As of June 15, 2025: A state discovers an intentional Program violation that began 30 months ago. How far back must the claim be calculated?
A. Only 6 months
B. Only to the start of the current certification period
C. To the month the violation first occurred
D. Only 12 months
E. Only 24 months

As of June 15, 2025: A state discovers an overpayment that started 8 years ago. What is the oldest period a claim may include?
A. Only the current certification period
B. The full 8 years
C. No amounts more than six years before the state became aware of it
D. Only 12 months
E. Only 3 years

As of June 15, 2025: A county error cost a household benefits for 18 months before the household asked for restoration. How many months of lost benefits must be restored (absent a rule allowing longer)?
A. All 18 months
B. Not more than 12 months
C. 6 months
D. None; only future benefits are adjusted
E. 3 months

As of November 1, 2024: A married couple live together but buy and cook food separately. How must they apply?
A. As two households, since they buy food separately
B. As two households only if one is elderly
C. As one household only if they have children
D. As one household: spouses must be in the same household
E. Either way, at their choice

As of November 1, 2024: A 23-year-old lives with his parents and buys and prepares his food separately. Must he be in his parents' household?
A. No: only people under 18 are covered
B. No: the required combination covers people under 22
C. Yes, if he is a student
D. Yes: adult children living with parents must be included
E. Yes, until age 25

As of November 1, 2024: A 16-year-old (not a foster child) lives with and is under the parental control of her grandmother, who receives SNAP. Must she be in her grandmother's household?
A. No: a 16-year-old may apply alone
B. Only if she has no income
C. Yes
D. No: only if the grandmother is her legal guardian
E. No: only parents and children must apply together

As of April 1, 2025: An employer provides an employee free housing instead of a cash payment. How is the value of the housing treated for SNAP?
A. Counted as earned income
B. Counted as a resource
C. Excluded: it is an in-kind benefit
D. Counted as unearned income
E. Counted at half its value

As of April 1, 2025: A household receives a payment that reimburses its normal rent. Is the reimbursement excluded from income?
A. Yes, if paid by a charity
B. Only if paid directly to the landlord
C. No: reimbursements for normal living expenses such as rent are a gain or benefit and are counted
D. Yes: all reimbursements are excluded
E. Yes, up to $100

As of April 1, 2025: A household member rents out a property and actively manages it 25 hours a week on average. How is the rental income treated?
A. As a resource only
B. As excluded income
C. As unearned income
D. As earned (self-employment) income
E. As income only above $500

As of April 1, 2025: A household receives payments from a roomer (not a foster care boarder). How are those payments treated?
A. As a resource
B. As unearned income
C. As a reduction of shelter costs
D. As excluded income
E. As self-employment income

As of April 1, 2025: A household member applied for a new job but it is uncertain whether or when the job will start. How is the possible income treated at certification?
A. Counted at the state minimum wage
B. Counted at the expected wage
C. Counted at half the expected wage
D. Not counted, because the amount or timing is uncertain
E. Counted only for the first month

As of April 1, 2025: A state uses the child support deduction. A household member voluntarily sends money to a non-household child without any legal obligation. Is it deductible?
A. Yes, if paid by check
B. Yes, up to $200
C. Yes: any support to a child is deductible
D. Only if the child is under 6
E. No: only legally obligated child support is deductible

As of April 1, 2025: A state uses the child support deduction. Are alimony payments a household member makes to a former spouse deductible under it?
A. Yes, up to the standard deduction
B. Only if the former spouse has children
C. No
D. Only if court ordered
E. Yes, in full

As of April 1, 2025: A household applies on April 10 and contains a member who is 59 on that date but turns 60 on April 25. Which income test applies for the application month?
A. Both gross and net income tests
B. The 165% gross income test
C. The net income test only (as for households with an elderly member)
D. The gross income test only
E. No income test

As of April 1, 2025: A household member is a student whose earnings are excluded because of age, and she turns 18 during the month of application. When are her earnings counted?
A. In the month of application
B. Starting the month after the month of application
C. Starting at the next recertification
D. Never, while she is a student
E. Starting the month she turns 19

As of April 1, 2025: An eligible one-person household applies mid-month. Does the minimum benefit guarantee apply to its prorated first month?
A. Yes, and it is doubled
B. Yes: the minimum benefit always applies
C. Only if the prorated amount is over $10
D. Only if the household is elderly
E. No: the minimum benefit applies except during an initial month

As of April 1, 2025: A state uses a standard 30-day month. A household applies on the 31st. For proration, it is treated as applying on which day?
A. The 29th
B. The 15th
C. The 31st
D. The 1st of the next month
E. The 30th

As of December 1, 2025: A simplified-reporting household of 3 had a fourth member join after certification. Which household size's gross income limit does it use to decide whether it must report higher income?
A. No limit; it reports only at recertification
B. 3, the size at its most recent certification
C. The larger of the two
D. The 165% limit for 4
E. 4, its current size

As of December 1, 2025: Between periodic reports, when must a simplified-reporting household report a change in income?
A. Whenever income changes by $50 or more
B. Only at recertification
C. Within 10 days of any change
D. Whenever income changes by $100 or more
E. When its monthly gross income exceeds the gross income limit (130% of poverty) for its size

As of May 1, 2026: A state certifies a household whose adult members are all elderly for 24 months. What contact must the state have during that period?
A. None until recertification
B. At least one contact every 12 months
C. A contact every 6 months
D. Monthly reports
E. A home visit every year

As of August 1, 2025: An applicant's employer refuses to cooperate and no other verification of the applicant's wages is available. What does the eligibility worker do?
A. Use the best available information to determine an amount for certification
B. Delay certification until the employer responds
C. Deny the application
D. Count income at 130% of poverty
E. Count zero income

As of March 1, 2025: How is the SNAP Quality Control error tolerance threshold adjusted each year?
A. By the percentage change in the Thrifty Food Plan
B. It is fixed at $37
C. By the change in the standard deduction
D. By the change in the national error rate
E. By the Consumer Price Index for shelter

As of March 1, 2025: What was the Quality Control error tolerance threshold for fiscal year 2014?
A. $38
B. $0
C. $25
D. $50
E. $37

As of January 20, 2025: Which of these people is exempt from the general SNAP work requirements because of age?
A. A 55-year-old
B. A 60-year-old
C. A 17-year-old head of household not in school
D. A 58-year-old
E. A 50-year-old

As of January 20, 2025: A 17-year-old who is not the head of household attends high school half-time. Are they exempt from the general SNAP work requirements?
A. No: they must work 20 hours
B. Only during summer
C. Yes
D. No: only people under 16 are exempt
E. Only if a parent is exempt
